name: GSK-971086
lead: GSK-971086 (also written GSK971086) is an investigational non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) from the indole chemical class, developed by GlaxoSmithKline and investigated for sarcopenia (age-related muscle loss) and androgen deficiency [1][2].

A Phase I trial registered in 2007 tested safety, tolerability and blood levels in healthy adult males after a single dose and after seven days of dosing [2]. Development was discontinued after Phase I [1]. No results for appearance or muscle-building have been published in the sources reviewed.

paras: Wikipedia lists GSK971086 as an indole-class SARM investigated for sarcopenia that did not progress beyond Phase I [1]. The only registered trial in the sources reviewed (NCT00540553) began in August 2007, enrolled 126 participants, and is listed as completed [2].

No SARM had been approved by the FDA or EMA as of 2023, and WADA has banned the class since 2008 [1]. Reported adverse effects of SARMs in trials have been described as mild and infrequent, while case reports link recreational use to drug-induced liver injury [1].

One Phase I trial (NCT00540553, n=126, healthy adult males, started 2007) examined safety, tolerability and blood levels after one dose and after seven days of dosing; it is listed as completed [2]. Results are not provided in the sources reviewed, and no efficacy trial has been reported.

timeline.event: Phase I safety and pharmacokinetic trial begins in healthy males. [2]

refs.title: Study to Test Safety, Tolerability and Blood Levels of GSK971086 After 1 Dose & 7 Days of Dosing in Healthy Adult Males (NCT00540553)

card.summary: A discontinued GSK indole-class SARM that never got past Phase I; no efficacy data exist.
card.note: Investigational only; not approved and no published efficacy results.

quick.overview:
GSK-971086 is an experimental SARM from GlaxoSmithKline that was studied for sarcopenia and androgen deficiency.

It was tested in a single Phase I safety trial in healthy men and then discontinued. It is not a marketed drug.
quick.mechanism: SARMs aim to switch on androgen receptors selectively, favoring muscle and bone over reproductive tissues. This compound belongs to the indole chemical class.
quick.risks: No results from its Phase I trial are public in the sources reviewed. The SARM class is unapproved, banned in sport by WADA, and linked in case reports to liver injury with recreational use.
